rules.title: CancellationToken Required
rules.check: All async methods performing I/O or long-running operations MUST accept a CancellationToken.

rules.title: CancellationToken Last Parameter
rules.check: CancellationToken MUST be the last parameter in the method signature.
rules.bad_example: public async Task Do(CancellationToken ct, int data) { ... }
rules.good_example: public async Task Do(int data, CancellationToken ct = default) { ... }

rules.title: Async Suffix
rules.check: Async methods MUST have the Async suffix (except controllers/event handlers).

rules.title: No Async Void
rules.check: async void is STRICTLY FORBIDDEN (except for top-level event handlers). It crashes the process on exception.

rules.title: ConfigureAwait(false) in Libraries
rules.check: Library code MUST use ConfigureAwait(false) to prevent context blocking.

rules.title: No Sync Over Async
rules.check: NEVER block on async code using .Result or .Wait(). It causes deadlocks.

rules.title: ValueTask Usage
rules.check: Use ValueTask<T> for hot path methods that often complete synchronously to reduce allocations.

rules.title: Async Disposal
rules.check: Classes with async cleanup MUST implement IAsyncDisposable and consumers MUST use await using.

rules.title: Timeout All HTTP Calls
rules.check: HTTP client calls MUST have a timeout configured.
rules.bad_example:
var http = new HttpClient();
await http.GetAsync(url); // May hang forever
rules.good_example:
var http = new HttpClient { Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30) };
await http.GetAsync(url, ct);

rules.title: Async Streams
rules.check: Use IAsyncEnumerable<T> for streaming data instead of returning Task<List<T>>.
